english.title: Release / market genetically modified organism without consent
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) contravened section 111(1) of the Environmental Protection Act 1990 in relation to something which was and you knew was or had reason to believe was a genetically modified organism in that you

(A)_[released]_
(B)_[marketed]_

it

(C)_[in such case or circumstances as were prescribed in relation to that act]_
(D)_[where you had been given directions under section 108(8)(a) of that Act]_

otherwise than in pursuance of a consent granted by the Secretary of State and in accordance with limitations and conditions to which the consent was subject
english.legislation: Contrary to sections 111(1) and 118(1)(c) and (3) of the Environmental Protection Act 1990.
english.pointstoprove:
date and location
released / market something
which was / believed to be
genetically modified organism
fail to obtain required consent / act outside consent

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes: Section 111(7) of the Environmental Protection Act 1990 provides that Regulations under this section may provide for exemptions, or for the granting by the Secretary of State, or by the Secretary of State and the Food Standards Agency acting jointly, of exemptions to particular persons or classes of person, from (a) any requirement under subsection (1) or (2) above to have a consent, or (b) any of the requirements to be fulfilled under the regulations by an applicant for a consent, in such cases or circumstances as may be prescribed.

other.penalty:
Summary: Six months imprisonment and / or a fine not exceeding twenty thousand pounds
Indictment: Five years imprisonment and / or a fine

Time limit for prosecutions:
None

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
